title: Swap with Pointers
statement: Read two integers `a` and `b`. Write a function `void swap(int *x, int *y)` that swaps them through pointers, call it, and print the values as `a b` after the swap.
outputFormat: Print the two values after swapping, separated by a space.
pseudocode:
FUNCTION swap(x, y)
  SET t = *x
  SET *x = *y
  SET *y = t
END FUNCTION
READ a, b
CALL swap(a, b)
PRINT "{a} {b}"
explanation:
## What the program does
Read two integers a and b. Write a function void swap(int *x, int *y) that swaps them through pointers, call it, and print the values as a b after the swap.

## The idea
A pointer holds the address of another variable. *p reads or writes the value at that address, and p + 1 moves to the next element of the same type.

## Step by step
1. Define the function swap(x, y):
   - Store *x in t.
   - Store *y in *x.
   - Store t in *y.
2. Read a, b from the input.
3. Run swap(a, b).
4. Print "{a} {b}".

## Example
For this input:
3 5

the program prints:

title: Shapes and Polymorphism
statement: Define an abstract class `Shape` with an abstract method `area()` and subclasses `Circle` (radius), `Square` (side) and `Rectangle` (width, height). Read `q` shapes and print each one's area with two decimals, one per line. Use `Math.PI`.
inputFormat: First line `q`. Then `q` lines: `circle r`, `square s` or `rectangle w h`.
outputFormat: One area per line, two decimals.
constraints: 1 <= q <= 100, values are positive integers up to 1000
pseudocode:
CLASS Shape
  abstract double area()
END CLASS
CLASS Circle EXTENDS Shape
  FUNCTION Circle(r)
    SET this.r = r
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION area()
    RETURN Math.PI * r * r
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
CLASS Square EXTENDS Shape
  FUNCTION Square(s)
    SET this.s = s
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION area()
    RETURN s * s
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
CLASS Rectangle EXTENDS Shape
  FUNCTION Rectangle(w, h)
    SET this.w = w
    SET this.h = h
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION area()
    RETURN w * h
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ q
FOR i FROM 0 TO q - 1
  READ kind
  SET s = kind.equals("circle") ? Circle(the next number read) : kind.equals("square") ? Square(the next number read) : Rectangle(the next number read, the next number read)
  PRINT "{s.area()}%n"
END FOR
explanation:
## What the program does
Define an abstract class Shape with an abstract method area() and subclasses Circle (radius), Square (side) and Rectangle (width, height). Read q shapes and print each one's area with two decimals, one per line. Use Math.PI.

## The idea
A subclass extends a parent class and can replace (override) its methods, so one type of reference can behave in many ways (polymorphism).

## Step by step
1. Define the class Shape:
   - Abstract double area().
2. Define the class Circle EXTENDS Shape:
   - Define the function Circle(r):
     - Store r in this.r.
   - Define the function area():
     - Give back Math.PI * r * r.
3. Define the class Square EXTENDS Shape:
   - Define the function Square(s):
     - Store s in this.s.
   - Define the function area():
     - Give back s * s.
4. Define the class Rectangle EXTENDS Shape:
   - Define the function Rectangle(w, h):
     - Store w in this.w.
     - Store h in this.h.
   - Define the function area():
     - Give back w * h.
5. Read q from the input.
6. Let i go from 0 up to q - 1, and for each value:
   - Read kind from the input.
   - Store kind.equals("circle") ? Circle(the next number read) : kind.equals("square") ? Square(the next number read) : Rectangle(the next number read, the next number read) in s.
   - Print "{s.area()}%n".

title: Reverse a Linked List
statement:
A singly linked list is given by its values from head to tail. Reverse the list and print the values from the new head to the new tail.

Try doing it by changing the `next` pointers instead of building a new list.
outputFormat: Print the reversed list, separated by spaces.
solution:
n = int(input())
values = input().split()
class Node:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.v, self.next = v, None
head = None
for v in reversed(values):
    node = Node(v)
    node.next = head
    head = node
prev = None
while head:
    nxt = head.next
    head.next = prev
    prev, head = head, nxt
out = []
while prev:
    out.append(prev.v)
    prev = prev.next
print(*out)
pseudocode:
READ n
READ values
CLASS Node
  FUNCTION __init__(self, v)
    SET self.v, self.next = v, nothing
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
SET head = nothing
FOR EACH v IN reversed(values)
  SET node = Node(v)
  SET node.next = head
  SET head = node
END FOR
SET prev = nothing
WHILE head
  SET nxt = head.next
  SET head.next = prev
  SET prev, head = head, nxt
END WHILE
SET out = an empty list
WHILE prev
  ADD prev.v TO out
  SET prev = prev.next
END WHILE
PRINT *out
explanation:
## What the program does
A singly linked list is given by its values from head to tail. Reverse the list and print the values from the new head to the new tail.

## The idea
A linked list is a chain of nodes where each node points to the next one; many tasks just walk or re-link those pointers.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Read values from the input.
3. Define the class Node:
   - Define the function __init__(self, v):
     - Store v, nothing in self.v, self.next.
4. Store nothing in head.
5. Go through every v in reversed(values), and for each one:
   - Store Node(v) in node.
   - Store head in node.next.
   - Store node in head.
6. Store nothing in prev.
7. Keep repeating while head:
   - Store head.next in nxt.
   - Store prev in head.next.
   - Store head, nxt in prev, head.
8. Store an empty list in out.
9. Keep repeating while prev:
   - ADD prev.v TO out.
   - Store prev.next in prev.
10. Print *out.

## Example
For this input:
5
1 2 3 4 5

the program prints:
5 4 3 2 1

title: BST In-order Traversal
statement: Insert the given values, in order, into an empty binary search tree (a value that is already present is ignored). Print the in-order traversal of the tree.
outputFormat: Print the in-order traversal separated by spaces.
solution:
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)
n = int(input())
values = list(map(int, input().split()))
root = None
for v in values:
    if root is None:
        root = [v, None, None]
        continue
    cur = root
    while True:
        if v == cur[0]:
            break
        side = 1 if v < cur[0] else 2
        if cur[side] is None:
            cur[side] = [v, None, None]
            break
        cur = cur[side]
out = []
def walk(node):
    if node:
        walk(node[1]); out.append(node[0]); walk(node[2])
walk(root)
print(*out)
pseudocode:
CALL sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)
READ n
READ list values
SET root = nothing
FOR EACH v IN values
  IF root is nothing THEN
    SET root = [v, nothing, nothing]
    CONTINUE
  END IF
  SET cur = root
  WHILE true
    IF v = cur[0] THEN
      BREAK
    END IF
    SET side = 1 if v < cur[0] else 2
    IF cur[side] is nothing THEN
      SET cur[side] = [v, nothing, nothing]
      BREAK
    END IF
    SET cur = cur[side]
  END WHILE
END FOR
SET out = an empty list
FUNCTION walk(node)
  IF node THEN
    CALL walk(node[1])
    ADD node[0] TO out
    CALL walk(node[2])
  END IF
END FUNCTION
CALL walk(root)
PRINT *out
explanation:
## What the program does
Insert the given values, in order, into an empty binary search tree (a value that is already present is ignored). Print the in-order traversal of the tree.

## The idea
A tree is nodes with children. Most tree tasks are recursive: handle the node, then do the same for the left and right child.

## Step by step
1. Run sys.setrecursionlimit(100000).
2. Read n from the input.
3. Read list values from the input.
4. Store nothing in root.
5. Go through every v in values, and for each one:
   - If root is nothing:
     - Store [v, nothing, nothing] in root.
     - Skip to the next pass.
   - Store root in cur.
   - Keep repeating while true:
     - If v = cur[0]:
       - Leave the loop.
     - Store 1 if v < cur[0] else 2 in side.
     - If cur[side] is nothing:
       - Store [v, nothing, nothing] in cur[side].
       - Leave the loop.
     - Store cur[side] in cur.
6. Store an empty list in out.
7. Define the function walk(node):
   - If node:
     - Run walk(node[1]).
     - ADD node[0] TO out.
     - Run walk(node[2]).
8. Run walk(root).
9. Print *out.

## Example
For this input:
5
5 3 8 1 4

the program prints:
1 3 4 5 8

title: Shortest Path in a Graph (BFS)
statement: An undirected, unweighted graph has `n` nodes numbered `1..n`. Print the minimum number of edges on a path from node `s` to node `t`, or `-1` if `t` cannot be reached.
inputFormat: First line `n m`. Then `m` lines `u v` (an edge). Last line `s t`.
solution:
from collections import deque
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    g[u].append(v); g[v].append(u)
s, t = map(int, input().split())
dist = [-1] * (n + 1)
dist[s] = 0
q = deque([s])
while q:
    u = q.popleft()
    for v in g[u]:
        if dist[v] < 0:
            dist[v] = dist[u] + 1
            q.append(v)
print(dist[t])
pseudocode:
READ n, m
SET g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
FOR _ FROM 0 TO m - 1
  READ u, v
  ADD v TO g[u]
  ADD u TO g[v]
END FOR
READ s, t
SET dist = [-1] * (n + 1)
SET dist[s] = 0
SET q = deque([s])
WHILE q
  SET u = q.popleft()
  FOR EACH v IN g[u]
    IF dist[v] < 0 THEN
      SET dist[v] = dist[u] + 1
      ADD v TO q
    END IF
  END FOR
END WHILE
PRINT dist[t]
explanation:
## What the program does
An undirected, unweighted graph has n nodes numbered 1..n. Print the minimum number of edges on a path from node s to node t, or -1 if t cannot be reached.

## The idea
A graph is points (nodes) joined by edges. Breadth-first search visits nodes level by level using a queue; depth-first search goes as deep as it can using a stack or recursion.

## Step by step
1. Read n, m from the input.
2. Store [[] for _ in range(n + 1)] in g.
3. Let _ go from 0 up to m - 1, and for each value:
   - Read u, v from the input.
   - ADD v TO g[u].
   - ADD u TO g[v].
4. Read s, t from the input.
5. Store [-1] * (n + 1) in dist.
6. Store 0 in dist[s].
7. Store deque([s]) in q.
8. Keep repeating while q:
   - Store q.popleft() in u.
   - Go through every v in g[u], and for each one:
     - If dist[v] < 0:
       - Store dist[u] + 1 in dist[v].
       - ADD v TO q.
9. Print dist[t].

## Example
For this input:
5 5
1 2
2 3
3 4
4 5
1 5
1 4

the program prints:
2

title: Queue Using Two Stacks
statement:
Simulate a first-in-first-out queue using only two stacks. Process the operations in order:
- `push x` adds `x` to the back.
- `pop` removes the front and prints it.
- `front` prints the front without removing it.

If the queue is empty, `pop` and `front` print `EMPTY`.
pseudocode:
READ q
SET in_stack, out_stack = [], []
FUNCTION shift()
  IF NOT out_stack THEN
    WHILE in_stack
      ADD in_stack.pop() TO out_stack
    END WHILE
  END IF
END FUNCTION
FOR _ FROM 0 TO q - 1
  READ parts
  IF parts[0] = 'push' THEN
    ADD parts[1] TO in_stack
  ELSE
    CALL shift()
    IF NOT out_stack THEN
      PRINT 'EMPTY'
    ELSE IF parts[0] = 'pop' THEN
      PRINT out_stack.pop()
    ELSE
      PRINT out_stack[-1]
    END IF
  END IF
END FOR
explanation:
## What the program does
Simulate a first-in-first-out queue using only two stacks. Process the operations in order: - push x adds x to the back. - pop removes the front and prints it. - front prints the front without removing it.

## The idea
A stack is last in, first out; a queue is first in, first out. Picking the right one often solves the problem.

## Step by step
1. Read q from the input.
2. Store [], [] in in_stack, out_stack.
3. Define the function shift():
   - If NOT out_stack:
     - Keep repeating while in_stack:
       - ADD in_stack.pop() TO out_stack.
4. Let _ go from 0 up to q - 1, and for each value:
   - Read parts from the input.
   - If parts[0] = 'push':
     - ADD parts[1] TO in_stack.
   - Otherwise:
     - Run shift().
     - If NOT out_stack:
       - Print 'EMPTY'.
     - Otherwise, if parts[0] = 'pop':
       - Print out_stack.pop().
     - Otherwise:
       - Print out_stack[-1].

pop

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
statement: Given `n` intervals `[a, b]`, merge every group of overlapping intervals (intervals that only touch, like `[1,3]` and `[3,5]`, also merge). Print the merged intervals in increasing order, one per line as `a b`.
inputFormat: First line `n`. Then `n` lines `a b` with `a <= b`.
outputFormat: Print the merged intervals, one per line.
pseudocode:
READ n
READ list items
SET out = an empty list
FOR EACH a, b IN items
  IF out AND a <= out[-1][1] THEN
    SET out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], b)
  ELSE
    ADD [a, b] TO out
  END IF
END FOR
FOR EACH a, b IN out
  PRINT a, b
END FOR
explanation:
## What the program does
Given n intervals [a, b], merge every group of overlapping intervals (intervals that only touch, like [1,3] and [3,5], also merge). Print the merged intervals in increasing order, one per line as a b.

## The idea
Sorting puts items in order so later steps (search, compare, merge) become easy.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Read list items from the input.
3. Store an empty list in out.
4. Go through every a, b in items, and for each one:
   - If out AND a <= out[-1][1]:
     - Store max(out[-1][1], b) in out[-1][1].
   - Otherwise:
     - ADD [a, b] TO out.
5. Go through every a, b in out, and for each one:
   - Print a, b.

## Example
For this input:
4
1 3
2 6
8 10
15 18

the program prints:
1 6
8 10
15 18

title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Given `n` integers and a number `k`, print the `k` values that occur most often. Order them by frequency (highest first); values with equal frequency are ordered by the smaller value first.
inputFormat: First line `n`. Second line `n` integers. Third line `k`.
constraints: 1 <= k <= number of distinct values <= n <= 10^5
solution:
from collections import Counter
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
k = int(input())
count = Counter(a)
print(*[v for v, _ in sorted(count.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:k]])
pseudocode:
READ n
READ list a
READ k
SET count = Counter(a)
PRINT *[v for v, _ in sorted(count.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:k]]
explanation:
## What the program does
Given n integers and a number k, print the k values that occur most often. Order them by frequency (highest first); values with equal frequency are ordered by the smaller value first.

## The idea
A dictionary (hash map) finds a value by its key in about one step, which makes counting and look-ups fast.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Read list a from the input.
3. Read k from the input.
4. Store Counter(a) in count.
5. Print *[v for v, _ in sorted(count.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:k]].

1 1 1 2 2 3

the program prints:

title: Detect a Cycle in a Directed Graph
statement: A directed graph has `n` nodes (`1..n`) and `m` edges `u -> v`. Print `Cycle` if the graph contains a directed cycle, otherwise print `No cycle`. (Hint: try Kahn's topological sort.)
inputFormat: First line `n m`. Then `m` lines `u v`.
solution:
from collections import deque
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
indeg = [0] * (n + 1)
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    g[u].append(v); indeg[v] += 1
q = deque(i for i in range(1, n + 1) if indeg[i] == 0)
seen = 0
while q:
    u = q.popleft(); seen += 1
    for v in g[u]:
        indeg[v] -= 1
        if indeg[v] == 0:
            q.append(v)
print('No cycle' if seen == n else 'Cycle')
pseudocode:
READ n, m
SET g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
SET indeg = [0] * (n + 1)
FOR _ FROM 0 TO m - 1
  READ u, v
  ADD v TO g[u]
  SET indeg[v] = indeg[v] + 1
END FOR
SET q = deque(i for i in range(1, n + 1) if indeg[i] = 0)
SET seen = 0
WHILE q
  SET u = q.popleft()
  SET seen = seen + 1
  FOR EACH v IN g[u]
    SET indeg[v] = indeg[v] - 1
    IF indeg[v] = 0 THEN
      ADD v TO q
    END IF
  END FOR
END WHILE
PRINT 'No cycle' if seen = n else 'Cycle'
explanation:
## What the program does
A directed graph has n nodes (1..n) and m edges u -> v. Print Cycle if the graph contains a directed cycle, otherwise print No cycle. (Hint: try Kahn's topological sort.)

## The idea
A graph is points (nodes) joined by edges. Breadth-first search visits nodes level by level using a queue; depth-first search goes as deep as it can using a stack or recursion.

## Step by step
1. Read n, m from the input.
2. Store [[] for _ in range(n + 1)] in g.
3. Store [0] * (n + 1) in indeg.
4. Let _ go from 0 up to m - 1, and for each value:
   - Read u, v from the input.
   - ADD v TO g[u].
   - Add 1 to indeg[v].
5. Store deque(i for i in range(1, n + 1) if indeg[i] = 0) in q.
6. Store 0 in seen.
7. Keep repeating while q:
   - Store q.popleft() in u.
   - Add 1 to seen.
   - Go through every v in g[u], and for each one:
     - Store indeg[v] - 1 in indeg[v].
     - If indeg[v] = 0:
       - ADD v TO q.
8. Print 'No cycle' if seen = n else 'Cycle'.

## Example
For this input:
3 3
1 2
2 3
3 1

the program prints:
Cycle

title: Next Greater Element
statement: For every element of an array, print the first element to its right that is strictly greater, or `-1` if there is none. A stack solves it in one pass.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
res = [-1] * n
stack = []
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    while stack and a[stack[-1]] < x:
        res[stack.pop()] = x
    stack.append(i)
print(*res)
pseudocode:
READ n
READ list a
SET res = [-1] * n
SET stack = an empty list
FOR EACH i, x IN enumerate(a)
  WHILE stack AND a[stack[-1]] < x
    SET res[stack.pop()] = x
  END WHILE
  ADD i TO stack
END FOR
PRINT *res
explanation:
## What the program does
For every element of an array, print the first element to its right that is strictly greater, or -1 if there is none. A stack solves it in one pass.

## The idea
A stack is last in, first out; a queue is first in, first out. Picking the right one often solves the problem.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Read list a from the input.
3. Store [-1] * n in res.
4. Store an empty list in stack.
5. Go through every i, x in enumerate(a), and for each one:
   - Keep repeating while stack AND a[stack[-1]] < x:
     - Store x in res[stack.pop()].
   - ADD i TO stack.
6. Print *res.

## Example
For this input:
4
4 5 2 25

the program prints:
5 25 25 -1

A variable is a named place in memory. Where it is declared decides who can see it (its scope) and how long it lives (its storage class).

title: The auto Storage Class
statement: Local variables are `auto` by default; the keyword can be written out: `auto int a`. Read two integers into `auto` variables and print `Sum: <a+b>` and `Product: <a*b>`.

READ a, b

explanation:
## What the program does
Local variables are auto by default; the keyword can be written out: auto int a. Read two integers into auto variables and print Sum: <a+b> and Product: <a*b>.

## The idea
A variable is a named place in memory. Where it is declared decides who can see it (its scope) and how long it lives (its storage class).

## Step by step
1. Read a, b from the input.
2. Print "Sum: {a + b} / Product: {a * b}".

FOR i FROM 1 TO n
  SET sum = sum + i
END FOR

title: Always Initialise
statement: A local variable that is never given a value holds a *garbage value*, so printing it gives unpredictable output. The fix is to start every accumulator at a known value. Read `n` integers and add them to `total`, which you **initialise to 0**. Print `Total: <total>`.
pseudocode:
SET total = 0
READ n
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  READ x
  SET total = total + x
END FOR
PRINT "Total: {total}"
explanation:
## What the program does
A local variable that is never given a value holds a *garbage value*, so printing it gives unpredictable output. The fix is to start every accumulator at a known value. Read n integers and add them to total, which you initialise to 0. Print Total: <total>.

## The idea
A variable is a named place in memory. Where it is declared decides who can see it (its scope) and how long it lives (its storage class).

## Step by step
1. Store 0 in total.
2. Read n from the input.
3. Let i go from 0 up to n - 1, and for each value:
   - Read x from the input.
   - Store total + x in total.
4. Print "Total: {total}".

    END IF

    IF q MOD i = 0 THEN

    BREAK
  END IF

title: Armstrong Function
statement: Write `int isArmstrong(int n)`: the digits, each raised to the number of digits, add up to `n`. Print `Yes` or `No`.
pseudocode:
FUNCTION isArmstrong(n)
  SET digits = 0
  FOR t FROM n WHILE t > 0 (SET t = t / 10)
    INCREASE digits BY 1
  END FOR
  SET sum = 0
  FOR t FROM n WHILE t > 0 (SET t = t / 10)
    SET p = 1
    FOR i FROM 0 TO digits - 1
      SET p = p * t MOD 10
    END FOR
    SET sum = sum + p
  END FOR
  RETURN sum = n
END FUNCTION
READ n
PRINT isArmstrong(n) ? "Yes" : "No"

   - Store 0 in digits.
   - FOR t FROM n WHILE t > 0 (SET t = t / 10).
     - Add 1 to digits.
   - Store 0 in sum.
   - FOR t FROM n WHILE t > 0 (SET t = t / 10).
     - Store 1 in p.
     - Let i go from 0 up to digits - 1, and for each value:
       - Store p * t MOD 10 in p.
     - Store sum + p in sum.
   - Give back sum = n.

title: Spiral Order
statement: Print the elements in spiral order (right along the top row, down the right column, left along the bottom row, up the left column, then inward) on one line.
inputFormat: First line `r c`, then the matrix.

    SET first = 0

  DECREASE right BY 1

      PRINT a[bottom][j]
    END FOR
    DECREASE bottom BY 1
  END IF
  IF left <= right THEN

      PRINT a[i][left]

    INCREASE left BY 1
  END IF
END WHILE

title: Read Lines of Any Length
statement: Read lines until the input ends. Each line may be long, so read it with a buffer that grows with `realloc`. For every line print `Line <k>: <length>` (k from 1, length without the newline).
constraints: At most 1000 lines of at most 5000 characters
pseudocode:

SET cap = 8
SET len = 0
SET buf = malloc(cap)
WHILE (c = getchar()) ≠ EOF
  IF c = '\n' THEN
    PRINT "Line {++lineNo}: {len}"
    SET len = 0
    CONTINUE
  END IF
  IF len + 1 >= cap THEN
    SET cap = cap * 2
    SET buf = realloc(buf, cap)
  END IF
  SET buf[len++] = c
END WHILE
IF len > 0 THEN
  PRINT "Line {++lineNo}: {len}"
END IF
FREE buf

statement: Read `n`, allocate `n` blocks and free only the ones with an even index (0, 2, 4, ...). Keep two counters and print `Allocated: <n>`, `Freed: <f>` and `Still allocated: <n - f>` (those are leaked memory). Free the rest at the very end so your program itself stays clean.

title: A Growing Stack
statement: Build a stack in an array that starts with room for 2 and doubles (`realloc`) when full. Read `n` commands: `push x` or `pop`. A `pop` on an empty stack prints `Stack empty`. After all commands print the stack from top to bottom on one line (or `Empty`).
outputFormat: Any error lines, then the final stack.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET cap = 2
SET top = 0
SET st = malloc(cap * sizeof(int))
WHILE n--
  READ cmd
  IF cmd[1] = 'u' THEN
    READ x
    IF top = cap THEN
      SET cap = cap * 2
      SET st = realloc(st, cap * sizeof(int))
    END IF
    SET st[top++] = x
  ELSE IF top = 0 THEN
    PRINT "Stack empty"
  ELSE
    DECREASE top BY 1
  END IF
END WHILE
IF top = 0 THEN
  PRINT "Empty"
END IF
FOR i FROM top - 1 DOWN TO 0
  PRINT st[i]
END FOR
FREE st
explanation:
## What the program does
Build a stack in an array that starts with room for 2 and doubles (realloc) when full. Read n commands: push x or pop. A pop on an empty stack prints Stack empty. After all commands print the stack from top to bottom on one line (or Empty).

## The idea
Linked lists, stacks, queues and trees are built from nodes allocated on the heap and connected by pointers. Each node you create must be freed when you are done.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Store 2 in cap.
3. Store 0 in top.
4. Store malloc(cap * sizeof(int)) in st.
5. Keep repeating while n--:
   - Read cmd from the input.
   - If cmd[1] = 'u':
     - Read x from the input.
     - If top = cap:
       - Store cap * 2 in cap.
       - Store realloc(st, cap * sizeof(int)) in st.
     - Store x in st[top++].
   - Otherwise, if top = 0:
     - Print "Stack empty".
   - Otherwise:
     - Subtract 1 from top.
6. If top = 0:
   - Print "Empty".
7. Count i down from top - 1 to 0, and for each value:
   - Print st[i].
8. Release the memory held by st.

title: A Linked Queue
statement: Build a queue from linked nodes. Read `n` commands: `enqueue x` or `dequeue`. Dequeuing from an empty queue prints `Queue empty`. After the commands print the queue from front to back on one line (or `Empty`).
outputFormat: Any error lines, then the final queue.
pseudocode:
STRUCTURE Node
  FIELD data
  FIELD next
END STRUCTURE
READ n
SET front = NULL
SET back = NULL
WHILE n--
  READ cmd
  IF cmd[0] = 'e' THEN
    SET node = malloc(sizeof(struct Node))
    READ node.data
    node.next = NULL
    IF back THEN
      back.next = node
    ELSE
      SET front = node
    END IF
    SET back = node
  ELSE IF NOT front THEN
    PRINT "Queue empty"
  ELSE
    SET old = front
    SET front = front.next
    IF NOT front THEN
      SET back = NULL
    END IF
    FREE old
  END IF
END WHILE
IF NOT front THEN
  PRINT "Empty"
END IF

  ELSE IF x < t.value THEN

  ELSE

  SET *first = 0

     - T.left = t.right = NULL.

   - Release the memory held by t.

   - Read x from the input.

title: An Allocation Registry
statement: Keep a table of live allocations. Read `n` commands: `alloc size` (gives the next id, starting at 1, and records the block) or `free id` (releases it; if the id is unknown or already freed print `Invalid free`). After the commands print `Active: <count>` and `Bytes: <total bytes still held>`.
outputFormat: Any error lines, then two lines.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET block = all zeros
SET size = all zeros
SET next = 1
WHILE n--
  READ cmd
  IF cmd[0] = 'a' THEN
    READ s
    SET block[next] = malloc(s)
    SET size[next++] = s
  ELSE
    READ id
    IF id < 1 OR id >= next OR block[id] = NULL THEN
      PRINT "Invalid free"
    ELSE
      FREE block[id]
      SET block[id] = NULL
      SET size[id] = 0
    END IF
  END IF
END WHILE
SET active = 0
SET bytes = 0
FOR i FROM 1 TO next - 1
  IF block[i] THEN
    INCREASE active BY 1
    SET bytes = bytes + size[i]
    FREE block[i]
  END IF
END FOR
PRINT "Active: {active} / Bytes: {bytes}"
explanation:
## What the program does
Keep a table of live allocations. Read n commands: alloc size (gives the next id, starting at 1, and records the block) or free id (releases it; if the id is unknown or already freed print Invalid free). After the commands print Active: <count> and Bytes: <total bytes still held>.

## The idea
Linked lists, stacks, queues and trees are built from nodes allocated on the heap and connected by pointers. Each node you create must be freed when you are done.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Store all zeros in block.
3. Store all zeros in size.
4. Store 1 in next.
5. Keep repeating while n--:
   - Read cmd from the input.
   - If cmd[0] = 'a':
     - Read s from the input.
     - Store malloc(s) in block[next].
     - Store s in size[next++].
   - Otherwise:
     - Read id from the input.
     - If id < 1 OR id >= next OR block[id] = NULL:
       - Print "Invalid free".
     - Otherwise:
       - Release the memory held by block[id].
       - Store NULL in block[id].
       - Store 0 in size[id].
6. Store 0 in active.
7. Store 0 in bytes.
8. Let i go from 1 up to next - 1, and for each value:
   - If block[i]:
     - Add 1 to active.
     - Store bytes + size[i] in bytes.
     - Release the memory held by block[i].
9. Print "Active: {active} / Bytes: {bytes}".

title: A Database that Grows and Shrinks
statement: Keep names in a dynamic array that starts with capacity 2. `add name` appends (double the capacity when full). `remove name` deletes the first match (print `Not found` if absent); after a removal, if `count * 4 <= capacity` and the capacity is above 2, halve the capacity. Read `n` commands and print `Names: ...` (or `Empty`), then `Count: <k>` and `Capacity: <c>`.
outputFormat: Any error lines, then three lines.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200, names have at most 30 characters
pseudocode:
READ n
SET cap = 2
SET count = 0
SET names = malloc(cap * sizeof(*names))
WHILE n--
  READ cmd, who
  IF cmd[0] = 'a' THEN
    IF count = cap THEN
      SET cap = cap * 2
      SET names = realloc(names, cap * sizeof(*names))
    END IF
    CALL strcpy(names[count++], who)
  ELSE
    SET at = -1
    FOR i FROM 0 TO count AND at < 0 - 1
      IF strcmp(names[i], who) = 0 THEN
        SET at = i
      END IF
    END FOR
    IF at < 0 THEN
      PRINT "Not found"
      CONTINUE
    END IF
    FOR i FROM at TO count - 1 - 1
      CALL strcpy(names[i], names[i + 1])
    END FOR
    DECREASE count BY 1
    IF count * 4 <= cap AND cap > 2 THEN
      SET cap = cap / 2
      SET names = realloc(names, cap * sizeof(*names))
    END IF
  END IF
END WHILE
IF count = 0 THEN
  PRINT "Empty"
ELSE
  PRINT "Names:"
  FOR i FROM 0 TO count - 1
    PRINT names[i]
  END FOR
  PRINT new line
END IF
PRINT "Count: {count} / Capacity: {cap}"
FREE names
explanation:
## What the program does
Keep names in a dynamic array that starts with capacity 2. add name appends (double the capacity when full). remove name deletes the first match (print Not found if absent); after a removal, if count * 4 <= capacity and the capacity is above 2, halve the capacity. Read n commands and print Names: ... (or Empty), then Count: <k> and Capacity: <c>.

## The idea
Linked lists, stacks, queues and trees are built from nodes allocated on the heap and connected by pointers. Each node you create must be freed when you are done.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Store 2 in cap.
3. Store 0 in count.
4. Store malloc(cap * sizeof(*names)) in names.
5. Keep repeating while n--:
   - Read cmd, who from the input.
   - If cmd[0] = 'a':
     - If count = cap:
       - Store cap * 2 in cap.
       - Store realloc(names, cap * sizeof(*names)) in names.
     - Run strcpy(names[count++], who).
   - Otherwise:
     - Store -1 in at.
     - Let i go from 0 up to count AND at < 0 - 1, and for each value:
       - If strcmp(names[i], who) = 0:
         - Store i in at.
     - If at < 0:
       - Print "Not found".
       - Skip to the next pass.
     - Let i go from at up to count - 1 - 1, and for each value:
       - Run strcpy(names[i], names[i + 1]).
     - Subtract 1 from count.
     - If count * 4 <= cap AND cap > 2:
       - Store cap / 2 in cap.
       - Store realloc(names, cap * sizeof(*names)) in names.
6. If count = 0:
   - Print "Empty".
7. Otherwise:
   - Print "Names:".
   - Let i go from 0 up to count - 1, and for each value:
     - Print names[i].
   - Print new line.
8. Print "Count: {count} / Capacity: {cap}".
9. Release the memory held by names.

Capacity: 4

title: The Builder Pattern
statement: `Pizza` is built step by step: `new Pizza.Builder().size(s).cheese(c).toppings(t).build()`. Its `toString()` is `<size> pizza, cheese: <yes/no>, toppings: <t>`. Read `size cheese toppings` (cheese is `true` or `false`) and print the pizza.

title: LinkedList as a Queue
statement: Use a `LinkedList` as a queue. Read `n` commands: `add x`, `poll` (remove and print the head, or `Empty`), `peek` (print the head without removing, or `Empty`). After all commands print `Size: <size>`.

pseudocode:

    PRINT head == null ? "Empty" : head
  END IF
END WHILE
PRINT "Size: " + q.size()

title: Your Own Linked List
statement: Build a singly linked list yourself (class `Node` plus a `MyList` with `addFirst`, `addLast` and `toString`). Read `n` commands `F x` (add at the front) or `L x` (add at the end) and print the list as `a -> b -> c`, or `Empty`.
pseudocode:
CLASS Node
  Node next
  FUNCTION Node(value)
    SET this.value = value
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
CLASS MyList
  Node head, tail
  FUNCTION addFirst(x)
    SET n = Node(x)
    SET n.next = head
    SET head = n
    IF tail = null THEN
      SET tail = n
    END IF
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION addLast(x)
    SET n = Node(x)
    IF tail = null THEN
      SET head = n
    ELSE
      SET tail.next = n
    END IF
    SET tail = n
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION toString()
    IF head = null THEN
      RETURN "Empty"
    END IF
    SET sb = StringBuilder()
    FOR (start with Node p = head; while p ≠ null; after each pass p = p.next)
      CALL sb.append(p.value).append(p.next ≠ null ? " => " : "")
    END FOR
    RETURN sb.toString()
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET list = MyList()
WHILE n-- > 0
  SET where = the next word read.charAt(0)
  READ x
  IF where = 'F' THEN

  ELSE
    CALL list.addLast(x)
  END IF
END WHILE

title: A Generic Queue
statement: Write your own `MyQueue<T>` with `enqueue`, `dequeue` (returns `null` when empty) and `size`, backed by a linked list of nodes. Read `n` integers, enqueue them all, then dequeue everything and print the numbers in order, separated by spaces, followed on the next line by `Size: <size>`.
pseudocode:
CLASS MyQueue
  CLASS Cell
    T value
    Cell next
    FUNCTION Cell(value)
      SET this.value = value
    END FUNCTION
  END CLASS
  private Cell head, tail
  FUNCTION enqueue(x)
    SET c = Cell(x)
    IF tail = null THEN
      SET head = c
    ELSE
      SET tail.next = c
    END IF
    SET tail = c
    INCREASE size BY 1
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION dequeue()
    IF head = null THEN
      RETURN null
    END IF
    SET v = head.value
    SET head = head.next
    IF head = null THEN
      SET tail = null
    END IF
    DECREASE size BY 1
    RETURN v
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION size()
    RETURN size
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET a = new int[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  READ a[i]
END FOR
SET q = MyQueue<>()
FOR int x : a
  CALL q.enqueue(x)
END FOR
SET sb = StringBuilder()
Integer x
WHILE (x = q.dequeue()) ≠ null
  IF sb.append(sb.length() > 0 THEN
    " "
  ELSE
    "").append(x)
  END IF
END WHILE
PRINT sb
PRINT "Size: " + q.size()

     - Store Cell(x) in c.

       - Store c in head.
     - Otherwise:
       - Store c in tail.next.
     - Store c in tail.
     - Add 1 to size.
   - Define the function dequeue():
     - If head = null:
       - Give back null.
     - Store head.value in v.
     - Store head.next in head.
     - If head = null:
       - Store null in tail.
     - Subtract 1 from size.
     - Give back v.
   - Define the function size():
     - Give back size.

title: Binary Search

inputFormat: Line 1 `n`, line 2 the sorted array, line 3 `key`.

title: Spiral Order
statement: Print the elements in spiral order (right along the top row, down the right column, left along the bottom row, up the left column, then inward) on one line.
inputFormat: First line `r c`, then the matrix.

  FOR j FROM 0 TO c - 1
    READ a[i][j]
  END FOR
END FOR
SET top = 0
SET bottom = r - 1
SET left = 0
SET right = c - 1
SET sb = StringBuilder()
WHILE top <= bottom AND left <= right
  FOR j FROM left TO right
    CALL sb.append(a[top][j]).append(" ")
  END FOR
  INCREASE top BY 1
  FOR i FROM top TO bottom
    CALL sb.append(a[i][right]).append(" ")
  END FOR
  DECREASE right BY 1
  IF top <= bottom THEN
    FOR j FROM right DOWN TO left
      CALL sb.append(a[bottom][j]).append(" ")
    END FOR
    DECREASE bottom BY 1
  END IF
  IF left <= right THEN
    FOR i FROM bottom DOWN TO top
      CALL sb.append(a[i][left]).append(" ")
    END FOR
    INCREASE left BY 1
  END IF
END WHILE
PRINT sb.toString().trim()

title: Flatten a Nested Array
statement: A nested array is written like `[1,[2,3],[4,[5]]]`. Write a recursive method that walks the text and prints the numbers in order on one line, separated by spaces.
pseudocode:
FUNCTION flatten(s, i, out)
  INCREASE i BY 1
  WHILE s.charAt(i) ≠ ']'
    SET c = s.charAt(i)
    IF c = '[' THEN
      SET i = flatten(s, i, out)
    ELSE IF c = ',' THEN
      INCREASE i BY 1
    ELSE
      SET j = i
      WHILE Character.isDigit(s.charAt(j))
        INCREASE j BY 1
      END WHILE
      CALL out.add(s.substring(i, j))
      SET i = j
    END IF
  END WHILE
  RETURN i + 1
END FUNCTION
READ s
SET out = ArrayList<>()
CALL flatten(s, 0, out)
PRINT String.join(" ", out)
explanation:
## What the program does
A nested array is written like [1,[2,3],[4,[5]]]. Write a recursive method that walks the text and prints the numbers in order on one line, separated by spaces.

## The idea
A recursive method solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller one. It needs a base case that stops the calls and a step that moves towards it.

## Step by step
1. Define the function flatten(s, i, out):
   - Add 1 to i.
   - Keep repeating while s.charAt(i) ≠ ']':
     - Store s.charAt(i) in c.
     - If c = '[':
       - Store flatten(s, i, out) in i.
     - Otherwise, if c = ',':
       - Add 1 to i.
     - Otherwise:
       - Store i in j.
       - Keep repeating while Character.isDigit(s.charAt(j)):
         - Add 1 to j.
       - Run out.add(s.substring(i, j)).
       - Store j in i.
   - Give back i + 1.
2. Read s from the input.
3. Store ArrayList<>() in out.
4. Run flatten(s, 0, out).
5. Print String.join(" ", out).

title: Waiting with join
statement: Split the sum `1 + 2 + ... + n` between three threads (thread `k` adds the numbers whose remainder when divided by 3 is `k`). Start all three, `join` all three, then print `Sum: <total>`.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET part = new long[3]
SET ts = Thread[3]
FOR k FROM 0 TO 3 - 1
  SET id = k
  SET ts[k] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    FOR i FROM 1 TO n
      IF i MOD 3 = id THEN
        SET part[id] = part[id] + i
      END IF
    END FOR
  ts[k].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread t : ts
  CALL t.join()
END FOR
PRINT "Sum: " + (part[0] + part[1] + part[2])

title: Thread States
statement: Create a thread that waits on a `CountDownLatch`. Print its state and `isAlive()` before `start()` (`NEW false`), then start it, wait until its state becomes `WAITING` and print `WAITING true`, release the latch, `join` and print `TERMINATED false`.
pseudocode:
SET latch = CountDownLatch(1)
SET t = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  TRY
    CALL latch.await()
  ON ERROR InterruptedException
  END TRY
PRINT t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive()
CALL t.start()
WHILE t.getState() ≠ Thread.State.WAITING
  CALL Thread.sleep(5)
END WHILE
PRINT t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive()
CALL latch.countDown()
CALL t.join()
PRINT t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive()

## The idea
A thread runs code at the same time as other threads. Start one with start(), wait for it with join(), and pass work to a thread pool with an ExecutorService.

1. Store CountDownLatch(1) in latch.
2. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in t.
   - Try the following:
     - Run latch.await().
   - If InterruptedException happens:
3. Print t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive().
4. Run t.start().
5. Keep repeating while t.getState() ≠ Thread.State.WAITING:
   - Run Thread.sleep(5).
6. Print t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive().
7. Run latch.countDown().
8. Run t.join().
9. Print t.getState() + " " + t.isAlive().

title: A Multi-Threaded Counter
statement: Start `t` threads that each add 1 to one shared counter `m` times. Make the increment `synchronized` so nothing is lost. After joining print `Count: <total>`.
pseudocode:

  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION get()

  END FUNCTION
END CLASS

SET ts = Thread[t]
FOR i FROM 0 TO t - 1
  SET ts[i] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    FOR j FROM 0 TO m - 1
      CALL c.increment()
    END FOR
  ts[i].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread x : ts
  CALL x.join()
END FOR
PRINT "Count: " + c.get()

   - Define the function get():
     - Give back count.

4. Store Thread[t] in ts.
5. Let i go from 0 up to t - 1, and for each value:
   - Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in ts[i].
     - Let j go from 0 up to m - 1, and for each value:
       - Run c.increment().

title: ScheduledExecutorService
statement: Schedule a task every 20 milliseconds with `scheduleAtFixedRate`. It prints `Tick <k>` and stops (the service shuts down) after the `n`th tick. Wait for it to finish and print `Ticks: <n>`.

  IF k <= n THEN
    PRINT "Tick " + k
    CALL done.countDown()
  END IF
  }, 0, 20, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  CALL done.await()
  CALL ses.shutdown()
  CALL ses.awaitTermination(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  PRINT "Ticks: " + n

statement: Simulate downloading `n` files. Read `n` and then the size in kilobytes of each file. Each file is "downloaded" by its own thread (sleep 5 ms, then add its size to a shared `AtomicLong`). After joining print `Files: <n>` and `Total: <KB> KB`.

title: Counting Threads in a Group
statement: Create a `ThreadGroup`, start `k` threads in it that wait on a `CountDownLatch`, and print `Active: <activeCount()>` once they are all waiting. Release them, join them and print `Active after: 0`.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET group = ThreadGroup("workers")
SET release = CountDownLatch(1)
SET started = CountDownLatch(n)
SET ts = Thread[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  SET ts[i] = Thread(group, () ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    CALL started.countDown()
    TRY
      CALL release.await()
    ON ERROR InterruptedException
    END TRY
  ts[i].start()
END FOR
CALL started.await()
PRINT "Active: " + group.activeCount()
CALL release.countDown()
FOR Thread t : ts
  CALL t.join()
END FOR
PRINT "Active after: " + group.activeCount()

title: A Race Condition, on Purpose
statement: Two threads each add 1 to a shared `int counter` with no lock. To make the lost update happen every time, force this order with two `Semaphore`s: thread A reads the counter, then lets B run; B adds 1 and writes it; A then writes `its old value + 1`. The counter ends at 1 instead of 2. Print `Counter: <value> (expected 2)`.
pseudocode:
SET counter = all zeros
SET aRead = Semaphore(0), bDone = Semaphore(0)
SET a = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  SET old = counter[0]
  CALL aRead.release()
  CALL bDone.acquireUninterruptibly()
  SET counter[0] = old + 1
SET b = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  CALL aRead.acquireUninterruptibly()
  SET counter[0] = counter[0] + 1
  CALL bDone.release()
CALL a.start()
CALL b.start()
CALL a.join()
CALL b.join()
PRINT "Counter: " + counter[0] + " (expected 2)"
explanation:
## What the program does
Two threads each add 1 to a shared int counter with no lock. To make the lost update happen every time, force this order with two Semaphores: thread A reads the counter, then lets B run; B adds 1 and writes it; A then writes its old value + 1. The counter ends at 1 instead of 2. Print Counter: <value> (expected 2).

## The idea
When threads share data they can overwrite each other's changes. Locks (synchronized, ReentrantLock) let one thread at a time in; wait/notify and BlockingQueue let threads hand work to each other.

## Step by step
1. Store all zeros in counter.
2. Store Semaphore(0), bDone = Semaphore(0) in aRead.
3. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in a.
   - Store counter[0] in old.
   - Run aRead.release().
   - Run bDone.acquireUninterruptibly().
   - Store old + 1 in counter[0].
4. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in b.
   - Run aRead.acquireUninterruptibly().
   - Add 1 to counter[0].
   - Run bDone.release().
5. Run a.start().
6. Run b.start().
7. Run a.join().
8. Run b.join().
9. Print "Counter: " + counter[0] + " (expected 2)".

## Example
The program prints:
Counter: 1 (expected 2)

title: A synchronized Block
statement: Two counters, `evens` and `odds`, each have their own lock object. `t` threads count the numbers `1..n` they are given (thread `k` takes `i % t == k`), adding to `evens` or `odds` inside a `synchronized (lock)` block. Print `Evens: <count>` and `Odds: <count>`.

READ t, n
SET evenLock = Object(), oddLock = Object()
SET counts = new int[2]
SET ts = Thread[t]
FOR k FROM 0 TO t - 1
  SET id = k
  SET ts[k] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    FOR i FROM 1 TO n
      IF i MOD t ≠ id THEN
        CONTINUE
      END IF
      IF i MOD 2 = 0 THEN
        FUNCTION synchronized(evenLock)
          INCREASE counts[0] BY 1
        END FUNCTION
      ELSE
        FUNCTION synchronized(oddLock)
          INCREASE counts[1] BY 1
        END FUNCTION
      END IF
    END FOR
  ts[k].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread x : ts
  CALL x.join()
END FOR
PRINT "Evens: " + counts[0]
PRINT "Odds: " + counts[1]

         - Skip to the next pass.
       - If i MOD 2 = 0:
         - Define the function synchronized(evenLock):
           - Add 1 to counts[0].
       - Otherwise:

           - Add 1 to counts[1].

title: Producer and Consumer with wait/notify
statement: A buffer holds one item. The producer thread puts `1..n` into it one at a time; the consumer takes them. Use `wait()` and `notifyAll()` in synchronized methods so the producer waits while the buffer is full and the consumer waits while it is empty. The consumer adds up what it takes. Print `Consumed sum: <sum>`.
pseudocode:
CLASS Buffer
  FUNCTION put(x)
    WHILE full
      TRY
        CALL wait()
      ON ERROR InterruptedException
        RETURN
      END TRY
    END WHILE
    SET item = x
    SET full = true
    CALL notifyAll()
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION take()
    WHILE NOT full
      TRY
        CALL wait()
      ON ERROR InterruptedException
        RETURN -1
      END TRY
    END WHILE
    SET full = false
    CALL notifyAll()
    RETURN item
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET buf = Buffer()
SET sum = new long[1]
SET producer = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 1 TO n
    CALL buf.put(i)
  END FOR
SET consumer = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 1 TO n
    SET sum[0] = sum[0] + buf.take()
  END FOR
CALL producer.start()
CALL consumer.start()
CALL producer.join()
CALL consumer.join()
PRINT "Consumed sum: " + sum[0]
explanation:
## What the program does
A buffer holds one item. The producer thread puts 1..n into it one at a time; the consumer takes them. Use wait() and notifyAll() in synchronized methods so the producer waits while the buffer is full and the consumer waits while it is empty. The consumer adds up what it takes. Print Consumed sum: <sum>.

## The idea
When threads share data they can overwrite each other's changes. Locks (synchronized, ReentrantLock) let one thread at a time in; wait/notify and BlockingQueue let threads hand work to each other.

## Step by step
1. Define the class Buffer:
   - Define the function put(x):
     - Keep repeating while full:
       - Try the following:
         - Run wait().
       - If InterruptedException happens:
         - Return from the function.
     - Store x in item.
     - Store true in full.
     - Run notifyAll().
   - Define the function take():
     - Keep repeating while NOT full:
       - Try the following:
         - Run wait().
       - If InterruptedException happens:
         - Give back -1.
     - Store false in full.
     - Run notifyAll().
     - Give back item.
2. Read n from the input.
3. Store Buffer() in buf.
4. Store new long[1] in sum.
5. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in producer.
   - Let i go from 1 up to n, and for each value:
     - Run buf.put(i).
6. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in consumer.
   - Let i go from 1 up to n, and for each value:
     - Store sum[0] + buf.take() in sum[0].
7. Run producer.start().
8. Run consumer.start().
9. Run producer.join().
10. Run consumer.join().
11. Print "Consumed sum: " + sum[0].

## Example
For this input:
5

the program prints:

CALL producer.start()
CALL consumer.start()
CALL producer.join()

title: ReadWriteLock
statement: A `ReentrantReadWriteLock` lets many readers in together but only one writer. A writer thread stores the value `v` under the write lock; after it has finished, `r` reader threads each read it under the read lock. Print `Readers saw: <v>` for each reader in order (collect the values first), then `Readers: <r>`.
pseudocode:
READ v, r
SET rw = ReentrantReadWriteLock()
SET value = all zeros
SET writer = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  CALL rw.writeLock().lock()
  TRY
    SET value[0] = v
  ALWAYS
    CALL rw.writeLock().unlock()
  END TRY
CALL writer.start()
CALL writer.join()
SET seen = new int[r]
SET readers = Thread[r]
FOR i FROM 0 TO r - 1
  SET id = i
  SET readers[i] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    CALL rw.readLock().lock()
    TRY
      SET seen[id] = value[0]
    ALWAYS
      CALL rw.readLock().unlock()
    END TRY
  readers[i].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread t : readers
  CALL t.join()
END FOR
FOR i FROM 0 TO r - 1
  PRINT "Readers saw: " + seen[i]
END FOR
PRINT "Readers: " + r

title: Semaphore Limits Access
statement: A `Semaphore` with 2 permits lets at most two threads use a resource together. Start 5 threads; each acquires a permit, records the number of threads currently inside (an `AtomicInteger`, keeping the maximum seen), sleeps 100 ms, and releases. After joining print `Max inside: <max>`.

      CALL sem.release()
    ON ERROR InterruptedException
    END TRY
  ts[i].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread t : ts
  CALL t.join()
END FOR
PRINT "Max inside: " + max.get()

title: Your Own Thread Pool
statement: Write a tiny pool: `w` worker threads take `Runnable` tasks from a `LinkedBlockingQueue`. Submit `n` tasks where task `i` stores `i * i` into slot `i` of a result array, then shut the pool down (send one stop signal per worker) and wait. Print `Result <i>: <value>` for `i = 1..n`.
pseudocode:
CLASS MiniPool
  SET private static final Runnable STOP = () ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  private final BlockingQueue<Runnable> queue = LinkedBlockingQueue<>()
  private final Thread[] workers
  FUNCTION MiniPool(n)
    SET workers = Thread[n]
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
      SET workers[i] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
        TRY
          WHILE true
            SET task = queue.take()
            IF task = STOP THEN
              RETURN
            END IF
            CALL task.run()
          END WHILE
        ON ERROR InterruptedException
        END TRY
      workers[i].start()
    END FOR
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION submit(r)
    CALL queue.add(r)
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION shutdownAndWait()
    FOR i FROM 0 TO workers.length - 1
      CALL queue.add(STOP)
    END FOR
    FOR Thread t : workers
      CALL t.join()
    END FOR
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ w, n
SET pool = MiniPool(w)
SET result = new int[n + 1]
FOR i FROM 1 TO n
  SET x = i
  CALL pool.submit(() => result[x] = x * x)
END FOR
CALL pool.shutdownAndWait()
FOR i FROM 1 TO n
  PRINT "Result " + i + ": " + result[i]
END FOR

     - Let i go from 0 up to n - 1, and for each value:
       - Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in workers[i].
         - Try the following:
           - Keep repeating while true:
             - Store queue.take() in task.
             - If task = STOP:
               - Return from the function.

         - If InterruptedException happens:
       - Workers[i].start().
   - Define the function submit(r):

2. Read w, n from the input.

title: Safe Bank Transfers
statement: Two accounts start with `a` and `b` rupees. Thread 1 moves 1 rupee from account 1 to account 2, `m` times; thread 2 moves 1 rupee from account 2 to account 1, `m` times. To avoid a deadlock both threads always lock the account with the **smaller id** first. Print `Account 1: <x>` and `Account 2: <y>` (the balances never go negative in the tests).
pseudocode:
CLASS Acct
  FUNCTION Acct(id, balance)
    SET this.id = id
    SET this.balance = balance
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION transfer(from, to, amount)
    SET first = from.id < to.id ? from : to, second = first = from ? to : from
    FUNCTION synchronized(first)
      FUNCTION synchronized(second)
        SET from.balance = from.balance - amount
        SET to.balance = to.balance + amount
      END FUNCTION
    END FUNCTION
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ a, b, m
SET x = Acct(1, a), y = Acct(2, b)
SET t1 = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 0 TO m - 1
    CALL Acct.transfer(x, y, 1)
  END FOR
SET t2 = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 0 TO m - 1
    CALL Acct.transfer(y, x, 1)
  END FOR
CALL t1.start()
CALL t2.start()
CALL t1.join()
CALL t2.join()
PRINT "Account 1: " + x.balance
PRINT "Account 2: " + y.balance

Two accounts start with a and b rupees. Thread 1 moves 1 rupee from account 1 to account 2, m times; thread 2 moves 1 rupee from account 2 to account 1, m times. To avoid a deadlock both threads always lock the account with the smaller id first. Print Account 1: <x> and Account 2: <y> (the balances never go negative in the tests).

## The idea
java.util.concurrent offers ready-made tools: CompletableFuture for asynchronous steps, ForkJoin for divide-and-conquer work, and building blocks for thread pools and worker queues.

## Step by step
1. Define the class Acct:

     - Store id in this.id.
     - Store balance in this.balance.
   - Define the function transfer(from, to, amount):
     - Store from.id < to.id ? from : to, second = first = from ? to : from in first.
     - Define the function synchronized(first):
       - Define the function synchronized(second):
         - Store from.balance - amount in from.balance.
         - Store to.balance + amount in to.balance.
2. Read a, b, m from the input.
3. Store Acct(1, a), y = Acct(2, b) in x.

5. Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in t2.

title: Counting Primes with Worker Threads
statement: Count the primes up to `n` with `w` worker threads: worker `k` checks the numbers `i` (from 2) with `i % w == k`, adding to its own count. Print `Primes up to <n>: <total>` after joining.
pseudocode:
READ w, n
SET part = new int[w]
SET ts = Thread[w]
FOR k FROM 0 TO w - 1
  SET id = k
  SET ts[k] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    FOR i FROM 2 TO n
      IF i MOD w ≠ id THEN
        CONTINUE
      END IF
      SET prime = true
      FOR d FROM 2 WHILE d * d <= i
        IF i MOD d = 0 THEN
          SET prime = false
          BREAK
        END IF
      END FOR
      IF prime THEN
        INCREASE part[id] BY 1
      END IF
    END FOR
  ts[k].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread t : ts
  CALL t.join()
END FOR
SET total = 0
FOR int c : part
  SET total = total + c
END FOR
PRINT "Primes up to " + n + ": " + total
explanation:
## What the program does
Count the primes up to n with w worker threads: worker k checks the numbers i (from 2) with i % w == k, adding to its own count. Print Primes up to <n>: <total> after joining.

## The idea
java.util.concurrent offers ready-made tools: CompletableFuture for asynchronous steps, ForkJoin for divide-and-conquer work, and building blocks for thread pools and worker queues.

## Step by step
1. Read w, n from the input.
2. Store new int[w] in part.
3. Store Thread[w] in ts.
4. Let k go from 0 up to w - 1, and for each value:
   - Store k in id.
   - Store Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE: in ts[k].
     - Let i go from 2 up to n, and for each value:
       - If i MOD w ≠ id:
         - Skip to the next pass.
       - Store true in prime.
       - FOR d FROM 2 WHILE d * d <= i.
         - If i MOD d = 0:
           - Store false in prime.
           - Leave the loop.
       - If prime:
         - Add 1 to part[id].
   - Ts[k].start().
5. FOR Thread t : ts.
   - Run t.join().
6. Store 0 in total.
7. FOR int c : part.
   - Store total + c in total.
8. Print "Primes up to " + n + ": " + total.

Primes up to 100: 25

title: A Worker Thread with a Queue
statement: One worker thread takes numbers from a `BlockingQueue`, squares them and appends the result to a list, until it takes the stop value `-1`. Put `n` numbers and then `-1` in the queue and print the results (in order) on one line after the worker ends.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET a = new int[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1

END FOR
SET q = LinkedBlockingQueue<>()
SET out = ArrayList<>()
SET worker = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  TRY
    WHILE (x = q.take()) ≠ -1
      CALL out.add(x * x)
    END WHILE
  ON ERROR InterruptedException
  END TRY
CALL worker.start()
FOR int x : a
  CALL q.put(x)
END FOR
CALL q.put(-1)
CALL worker.join()
PRINT out.toString().replaceAll("[\\[\\],]", "")

title: ForkJoinPool
statement: Add up `n` numbers with a `RecursiveTask<Long>`: a task for more than 4 numbers splits its range in two halves (`fork` one, `compute` the other, then `join`); small ranges are added directly. Run it in a `ForkJoinPool` and print `Sum: <total>`.
pseudocode:
CLASS SumTask EXTENDS RecursiveTask
  FUNCTION SumTask(a, lo, hi)
    SET this.a = a
    SET this.lo = lo
    SET this.hi = hi
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION compute()
    IF hi - lo <= 4 THEN
      SET s = 0
      FOR i FROM lo TO hi - 1
        SET s = s + a[i]
      END FOR
      RETURN s
    END IF
    SET mid = (lo + hi) / 2
    SET left = SumTask(a, lo, mid), right = SumTask(a, mid, hi)
    CALL left.fork()
    RETURN right.compute() + left.join()
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET a = new int[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  READ a[i]
END FOR
SET total = ForkJoinPool().invoke(SumTask(a, 0, n))
PRINT "Sum: " + total
explanation:
## What the program does
Add up n numbers with a RecursiveTask<Long>: a task for more than 4 numbers splits its range in two halves (fork one, compute the other, then join); small ranges are added directly. Run it in a ForkJoinPool and print Sum: <total>.

## The idea
java.util.concurrent offers ready-made tools: CompletableFuture for asynchronous steps, ForkJoin for divide-and-conquer work, and building blocks for thread pools and worker queues.

## Step by step
1. Define the class SumTask EXTENDS RecursiveTask:
   - Define the function SumTask(a, lo, hi):
     - Store a in this.a.
     - Store lo in this.lo.
     - Store hi in this.hi.
   - Define the function compute():
     - If hi - lo <= 4:
       - Store 0 in s.
       - Let i go from lo up to hi - 1, and for each value:
         - Store s + a[i] in s.
       - Give back s.
     - Store (lo + hi) / 2 in mid.
     - Store SumTask(a, lo, mid), right = SumTask(a, mid, hi) in left.
     - Run left.fork().
     - Give back right.compute() + left.join().
2. Read n from the input.
3. Store new int[n] in a.
4. Let i go from 0 up to n - 1, and for each value:
   - Read a[i] from the input.
5. Store ForkJoinPool().invoke(SumTask(a, 0, n)) in total.
6. Print "Sum: " + total.

title: Parallel Merge Sort
statement: Sort `n` numbers with a `RecursiveTask`: split the array in halves, sort each half in its own task (`fork` and `compute`), then merge the two sorted halves. Print the sorted numbers on one line.
pseudocode:
CLASS SortTask EXTENDS RecursiveTask
  FUNCTION SortTask(a)
    SET this.a = a
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION compute()
    IF a.length <= 1 THEN
      RETURN a
    END IF
    SET mid = a.length / 2
    SET left = SortTask(Arrays.copyOfRange(a, 0, mid)), right = SortTask(Arrays.copyOfRange(a, mid, a.length))
    CALL left.fork()
    SET r = right.compute()
    SET l = left.join()
    SET out = new int[a.length]
    SET i = 0
    SET j = 0
    SET k = 0
    WHILE i < l.length AND j < r.length
      SET out[k++] = l[i] <= r[j] ? l[i++] : r[j++]
    END WHILE
    WHILE i < l.length
      SET out[k++] = l[i++]
    END WHILE
    WHILE j < r.length
      SET out[k++] = r[j++]
    END WHILE
    RETURN out
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET a = new int[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  READ a[i]
END FOR
SET sorted = ForkJoinPool().invoke(SortTask(a))
SET sb = StringBuilder()
FOR i FROM 0 TO sorted.length - 1
  IF sb.append(sorted[i]).append(i < sorted.length - 1 THEN
    " "
  ELSE
    "")
  END IF
END FOR
PRINT sb
explanation:
## What the program does
Sort n numbers with a RecursiveTask: split the array in halves, sort each half in its own task (fork and compute), then merge the two sorted halves. Print the sorted numbers on one line.

## The idea
java.util.concurrent offers ready-made tools: CompletableFuture for asynchronous steps, ForkJoin for divide-and-conquer work, and building blocks for thread pools and worker queues.

## Step by step
1. Define the class SortTask EXTENDS RecursiveTask:
   - Define the function SortTask(a):
     - Store a in this.a.
   - Define the function compute():
     - If a.length <= 1:
       - Give back a.
     - Store a.length / 2 in mid.
     - Store SortTask(Arrays.copyOfRange(a, 0, mid)), right = SortTask(Arrays.copyOfRange(a, mid, a.length)) in left.
     - Run left.fork().
     - Store right.compute() in r.
     - Store left.join() in l.
     - Store new int[a.length] in out.
     - Store 0 in i.
     - Store 0 in j.
     - Store 0 in k.
     - Keep repeating while i < l.length AND j < r.length:
       - Store l[i] <= r[j] ? l[i++] : r[j++] in out[k++].
     - Keep repeating while i < l.length:
       - Store l[i++] in out[k++].
     - Keep repeating while j < r.length:
       - Store r[j++] in out[k++].
     - Give back out.
2. Read n from the input.
3. Store new int[n] in a.
4. Let i go from 0 up to n - 1, and for each value:
   - Read a[i] from the input.
5. Store ForkJoinPool().invoke(SortTask(a)) in sorted.
6. Store StringBuilder() in sb.
7. Let i go from 0 up to sorted.length - 1, and for each value:
   - If sb.append(sorted[i]).append(i < sorted.length - 1:
     - " ".
   - Otherwise:
     - "").
8. Print sb.

the program prints:

title: A Traffic Intersection
statement: Two threads, `North-South` and `East-West`, share an intersection and must take turns: North-South goes first. Each prints `<name> passes` when it is its turn, then hands over. They do this `n` times each. Use `wait()` and `notifyAll()` with a shared `turn` flag so the lines strictly alternate. After joining print `Cycles: <n>`.

        CALL wait()
      ON ERROR InterruptedException
        RETURN
      END TRY
    END WHILE
    PRINT name + " passes"
    SET turn = 1 - turn
    CALL notifyAll()
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET light = Light()
SET ns = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
    CALL light.pass(0, "North-South")
  END FOR
SET ew = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
    CALL light.pass(1, "East-West")
  END FOR
CALL ns.start()
CALL ew.start()
CALL ns.join()
CALL ew.join()
PRINT "Cycles: " + n

statement: Read a word, then the lines of a text. Save the lines to `search.txt`; read the file back and print the number of every line (starting at 1) that contains the word, each on one line as `Line <k>`; if none contains it print `Not found`. Delete the file.
inputFormat: First line the word; then any number of text lines.
pseudocode:

SET f = File("search.txt")

  WHILE in.hasNextLine()
    CALL w.println(the next line read)
  END WHILE
END TRY
SET found = false
TRY WITH r
  SET k = 0
  WHILE (line = r.readLine()) ≠ null
    INCREASE k BY 1
    IF line.contains(word) THEN

      SET found = true
    END IF

  PRINT "Not found"
END IF
CALL f.delete()

CALL a.delete()
CALL b.delete()

title: Custom writeObject and readObject
statement: Class `Secret` saves its `text` **reversed** by defining private `writeObject` and `readObject` methods (which call `defaultWriteObject`/`defaultReadObject` and handle the field themselves) so a saved file never holds the plain text. Read a word, save and load it and print `Restored: <word>` and `File holds reversed text: <true/false>` (search the bytes of the file for the reversed word).
pseudocode:
CLASS Secret
  SET serialVersionUID = 1L
  transient String text
  FUNCTION Secret(text)
    SET this.text = text
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION writeObject(out)
    CALL out.defaultWriteObject()
    CALL out.writeObject(StringBuilder(text).reverse().toString())
  END FUNCTION
  CALL in.defaultReadObject()
  SET text = StringBuilder((String) in.readObject()).reverse().toString()
END CLASS
READ w
SET f = File("secret.ser")
TRY WITH out
  CALL out.writeObject(Secret(w))
END TRY
SET raw = String(Files.readAllBytes(f.toPath()), StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1)
SET reversed = StringBuilder(w).reverse().toString()
TRY WITH inp
  PRINT "Restored: " + ((Secret) inp.readObject()).text
END TRY
PRINT "File holds reversed text: " + raw.contains(reversed)
CALL f.delete()
explanation:

Class Secret saves its text reversed by defining private writeObject and readObject methods (which call defaultWriteObject/defaultReadObject and handle the field themselves) so a saved file never holds the plain text. Read a word, save and load it and print Restored: <word> and File holds reversed text: <true/false> (search the bytes of the file for the reversed word).

Serialization turns an object into bytes you can store and later rebuild. NIO (Files, Path, channels) is the modern, more efficient way to work with files.

   - Transient String text.

     - Store text in this.text.
   - Define the function writeObject(out):
     - Run out.defaultWriteObject().
     - Run out.writeObject(StringBuilder(text).reverse().toString()).
   - Run in.defaultReadObject().
   - Store StringBuilder((String) in.readObject()).reverse().toString() in text.
2. Read w from the input.
3. Store File("secret.ser") in f.
4. Try the following, using out (they are closed automatically):
   - Run out.writeObject(Secret(w)).
5. Store String(Files.readAllBytes(f.toPath()), StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1) in raw.
6. Store StringBuilder(w).reverse().toString() in reversed.
7. Try the following, using inp (they are closed automatically):
   - Print "Restored: " + ((Secret) inp.readObject()).text.
8. Print "File holds reversed text: " + raw.contains(reversed).
9. Run f.delete().

title: Walk a Directory Tree
statement: Make the folder `tree` with the files `a.txt` and `sub/b.txt` and `sub/deep/c.txt` (and the folders in between). Use `Files.walk` to print every **file** path relative to `tree`, using `/`, sorted alphabetically, and `Files: <count>`. Delete the whole tree afterwards.
pseudocode:
SET root = Paths.get("tree")
CALL Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("sub/deep"))
CALL Files.write(root.resolve("a.txt"), "a".getBytes())
CALL Files.write(root.resolve("sub/b.txt"), "b".getBytes())
CALL Files.write(root.resolve("sub/deep/c.txt"), "c".getBytes())
SET files = ArrayList<>()
TRY WITH java.util.stream.Stream<Path> walk = Files.walk(root)
  CALL walk.filter(Files::isRegularFile).forEach(p => files.add(root.relativize(p).toString().replace(File.separatorChar, '/')))
END TRY
CALL Collections.sort(files)
FOR String f : files
  PRINT f
END FOR
PRINT "Files: " + files.size()
TRY WITH java.util.stream.Stream<Path> walk = Files.walk(root)
  SET all = ArrayList<>()
  CALL walk.forEach(all::add)
  CALL Collections.reverse(all)
  FOR Path p : all
    CALL Files.delete(p)
  END FOR
END TRY

title: Detect Directory Changes
statement: Real-time watching (`WatchService`) depends on the operating system, so do the same job by comparing snapshots. Make the folder `watch` with the files named on the first input line, take a snapshot of its names (a `Set`), then create the files named on the second line and delete the ones named on the third; take a second snapshot and print `Created: <sorted names>` and `Deleted: <sorted names>` (`none` when empty). Delete everything at the end.
inputFormat: Three lines: files that exist at the start, files to create, files to delete (each a space-separated list; a line with just `-` means none).
pseudocode:
SET dir = Paths.get("watch")
CALL Files.createDirectories(dir)
SET start = the next line read.trim().split("\\s+")
SET add = the next line read.trim().split("\\s+")
SET remove = the next line read.trim().split("\\s+")
FOR String n : start
  IF NOT n.equals("-") THEN
    CALL Files.write(dir.resolve(n), new byte[0])
  END IF
END FOR
SET before = TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(dir.toFile().list()))
FOR String n : add
  IF NOT n.equals("-") THEN
    CALL Files.write(dir.resolve(n), new byte[0])
  END IF
END FOR
FOR String n : remove
  IF NOT n.equals("-") THEN
    CALL Files.deleteIfExists(dir.resolve(n))
  END IF
END FOR
SET after = TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(dir.toFile().list()))
SET created = TreeSet<>(after), deleted = TreeSet<>(before)
CALL created.removeAll(before)
CALL deleted.removeAll(after)
PRINT "Created: " + (created.isEmpty() ? "none" : String.join(" ", created))
PRINT "Deleted: " + (deleted.isEmpty() ? "none" : String.join(" ", deleted))
FOR File f : dir.toFile().listFiles()
  CALL f.delete()
END FOR
CALL Files.delete(dir)

Real-time watching (WatchService) depends on the operating system, so do the same job by comparing snapshots. Make the folder watch with the files named on the first input line, take a snapshot of its names (a Set), then create the files named on the second line and delete the ones named on the third; take a second snapshot and print Created: <sorted names> and Deleted: <sorted names> (none when empty). Delete everything at the end.

## The idea
Serialization turns an object into bytes you can store and later rebuild. NIO (Files, Path, channels) is the modern, more efficient way to work with files.

## Step by step
1. Store Paths.get("watch") in dir.
2. Run Files.createDirectories(dir).
3. Store the next line read.trim().split("\\s+") in start.
4. Store the next line read.trim().split("\\s+") in add.
5. Store the next line read.trim().split("\\s+") in remove.
6. FOR String n : start.
   - If NOT n.equals("-"):
     - Run Files.write(dir.resolve(n), new byte[0]).
7. Store TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(dir.toFile().list())) in before.
8. FOR String n : add.
   - If NOT n.equals("-"):
     - Run Files.write(dir.resolve(n), new byte[0]).
9. FOR String n : remove.
   - If NOT n.equals("-"):
     - Run Files.deleteIfExists(dir.resolve(n)).
10. Store TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(dir.toFile().list())) in after.
11. Store TreeSet<>(after), deleted = TreeSet<>(before) in created.

13. Run deleted.removeAll(after).

title: FileChannel and ByteBuffer
statement: Write the bytes `1..n` to `chan.bin` with a `FileChannel` and a `ByteBuffer`, then read them back into a new buffer. Print `Read: <count> bytes` and `Sum: <sum of the bytes>`. Delete the file.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET p = Paths.get("chan.bin")
TRY WITH ch
  SET buf = ByteBuffer.allocate(n)
  FOR i FROM 1 TO n
    CALL buf.put((byte) i)
  END FOR
  CALL buf.flip()
  CALL ch.write(buf)
END TRY
SET sum = 0
TRY WITH ch
  SET buf = ByteBuffer.allocate(n)
  SET count = ch.read(buf)
  CALL buf.flip()
  WHILE buf.hasRemaining()
    SET sum = sum + buf.get()
  END WHILE
END TRY
PRINT "Read: " + count + " bytes"
PRINT "Sum: " + sum
CALL Files.delete(p)
explanation:
## What the program does
Write the bytes 1..n to chan.bin with a FileChannel and a ByteBuffer, then read them back into a new buffer. Print Read: <count> bytes and Sum: <sum of the bytes>. Delete the file.

## The idea
Serialization turns an object into bytes you can store and later rebuild. NIO (Files, Path, channels) is the modern, more efficient way to work with files.

## Step by step
1. Read n from the input.
2. Store Paths.get("chan.bin") in p.
3. Try the following, using ch (they are closed automatically):
   - Store ByteBuffer.allocate(n) in buf.
   - Let i go from 1 up to n, and for each value:
     - Run buf.put((byte) i).
   - Run buf.flip().
   - Run ch.write(buf).
4. Store 0 in sum.

title: A Multi-Client Chat Server
statement: The server accepts `n` clients, each in its own thread, and stores the line each client sends. `n` client threads connect and send the messages you read. After all of them finish print `Server received <n> messages` and then the messages sorted alphabetically, one per line.

READ n
SET w = String[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  READ w[i]
END FOR
SET server = ServerSocket(0)
SET received = Collections.synchronizedList(ArrayList<>())
SET acceptor = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  SET handlers = ArrayList<>()
  TRY
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
      SET s = server.accept()
      SET h = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
        TRY WITH s, r
          CALL received.add(r.readLine())
        ON ERROR IOException
        END TRY
      CALL h.start()
      CALL handlers.add(h)
    END FOR
    FOR Thread h : handlers
      CALL h.join()
    END FOR
  ON ERROR Exception
  END TRY
CALL acceptor.start()
SET clients = Thread[n]
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  SET msg = w[i]
  SET clients[i] = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
    CALL try(Socket c = Socket("127.0.0.1", server.getLocalPort())
    CALL out.println(msg)
  ON ERROR IOException
  clients[i].start()
END FOR
FOR Thread c : clients
  CALL c.join()
END FOR
CALL acceptor.join()
CALL server.close()
CALL Collections.sort(received)
PRINT "Server received " + received.size() + " messages"
FOR String m : received
  PRINT m
END FOR

title: A UDP Echo Server
statement: A server thread waits on a `DatagramSocket` (free port), receives one packet and sends back the text in capitals. In `main` send the word you read in a `DatagramPacket` and print `Server got: <word>` (printed by the server thread) after the reply has been received.
pseudocode:
READ word
SET serverSocket = DatagramSocket(0, InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1"))
SET got = String[1]
SET t = Thread(() ... WHERE THE STEPS ARE:
  TRY
    SET byte[] buf = new byte[256]
    SET p = DatagramPacket(buf, buf.length)
    CALL serverSocket.receive(p)
    SET got[0] = String(p.getData(), 0, p.getLength(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
    SET byte[] reply = got[0].toUpperCase().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
    CALL serverSocket.send(DatagramPacket(reply, reply.length, p.getAddress(), p.getPort()))
  ON ERROR IOException
  END TRY
CALL t.start()
TRY WITH client
  SET byte[] out = word.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
  CALL client.send(DatagramPacket(out, out.length, InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1"), serverSocket.getLocalPort()))
  CALL client.setSoTimeout(5000)
  SET in2 = DatagramPacket(new byte[256], 256)
  CALL client.receive(in2)
END TRY
CALL t.join()
PRINT "Server got: " + got[0]

title: A Port Scanner
statement: Open `k` server sockets on free ports, then scan these ports plus one port you bound and closed again. For each port try `new Socket()` with `connect(..., 300 ms)`; a successful connect means open. Print `Open: <count>` and `Closed: <count>`.
pseudocode:
READ n
SET servers = ArrayList<>()
SET ports = ArrayList<>()
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  SET s = ServerSocket(0)
  CALL servers.add(s)
  CALL ports.add(s.getLocalPort())
END FOR
SET temp = ServerSocket(0)
CALL ports.add(temp.getLocalPort())
CALL temp.close()
SET open = 0
SET closed = 0
FOR int port : ports
  TRY WITH s
    CALL s.connect(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", port), 300)
    INCREASE open BY 1
  ON ERROR IOException
    INCREASE closed BY 1
  END TRY
END FOR
PRINT "Open: " + open
PRINT "Closed: " + closed
FOR ServerSocket s : servers
  CALL s.close()
END FOR

title: A Secure Connection (Simulation)
statement: A real SSL/TLS handshake needs certificates, so simulate the idea of a secure channel: client and server share a secret; the client sends `message` together with its `HmacSHA256` signature; the server recomputes the signature and accepts only if they match. Read `secret message tamper` (`tamper` is `yes` or `no`; `yes` changes the message after signing). Print `Handshake OK`, then `Verified: <true/false>`.
pseudocode:
FUNCTION hmac(secret, text)
  SET mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256")
  CALL mac.init(SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), "HmacSHA256"))
  SET sb = StringBuilder()
  FOR byte b : mac.doFinal(text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
    CALL sb.append(String.format("%02x", b))
  END FOR
  RETURN sb.toString()
END FUNCTION
READ secret, message, tamper
SET sig = hmac(secret, message)
SET received = tamper.equals("yes") ? message + "NOT " : message
PRINT "Handshake OK"
PRINT "Verified: " + hmac(secret, received).equals(sig)

title: Key-Value Nodes in a Chain
statement: Write `class KV<K, V>` (a node with key, value and `next`) and a tiny map `ChainMap<K, V>` that keeps nodes in a chain: `put` replaces the value of an existing key or adds a node at the end; `get` returns the value or `null`. Read `n` pairs `word number`, then a word to look up, and print the stored number or `missing`.
inputFormat: Line 1 `n`, then `n` pairs, then a word.
pseudocode:
CLASS KV
  K key
  V value
  KV<K, V> next
  FUNCTION KV(key, value)
    SET this.key = key
    SET this.value = value
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
CLASS ChainMap
  private KV<K, V> head, tail
  FUNCTION put(key, value)
    FOR (start with KV<K, V> p = head; while p ≠ null; after each pass p = p.next)
      IF p.key.equals(key) THEN
        SET p.value = value
        RETURN
      END IF
    END FOR
    SET node = KV<>(key, value)
    IF tail = null THEN
      SET head = node
    ELSE
      SET tail.next = node
    END IF
    SET tail = node
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION get(key)
    FOR (start with KV<K, V> p = head; while p ≠ null; after each pass p = p.next)
      IF p.key.equals(key) THEN
        RETURN p.value
      END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN null
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET map = ChainMap<>()
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  CALL map.put(the next word read, the next number read)
END FOR
SET v = map.get(the next word read)
PRINT v == null ? "missing" : String.valueOf(v)

title: A Generic Binary Search Tree
statement: Write `class BST<T extends Comparable<T>>` with `insert` and `inOrder()` (a `List<T>`). Read `n` integers and `n` words, put each group in its own tree, and print the in-order contents of both on two lines (repeats are kept, going to the right).
pseudocode:
CLASS BST
  CLASS Node
    T value
    Node left, right
    FUNCTION Node(value)
      SET this.value = value
    END FUNCTION
  END CLASS
  private Node root
  FUNCTION insert(x)
    SET root = insert(root, x)
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION insert(n, x)
    IF n = null THEN
      RETURN Node(x)
    END IF
    IF x.compareTo(n.value) < 0 THEN
      SET n.left = insert(n.left, x)
    ELSE
      SET n.right = insert(n.right, x)
    END IF
    RETURN n
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION inOrder()
    SET out = ArrayList<>()
    CALL walk(root, out)
    RETURN out
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION walk(n, out)
    IF n = null THEN
      RETURN
    END IF
    CALL walk(n.left, out)
    CALL out.add(n.value)
    CALL walk(n.right, out)
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
READ n
SET a = BST<>()
SET b = BST<>()
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  CALL a.insert(the next number read)
END FOR
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  CALL b.insert(the next word read)
END FOR
PRINT a.inOrder().toString().replaceAll("[\\[\\],]", "")
PRINT b.inOrder().toString().replaceAll("[\\[\\],]", "")

title: A Logging Framework with Callbacks
statement: Write `class Logger` that holds a list of `Consumer<String>` handlers and a minimum level (`INFO` < `WARN` < `ERROR`). `log(level, text)` sends `[<LEVEL>] <text>` to every handler when the level is at least the minimum. Read the minimum level, then `n` lines `LEVEL text` (text is one word); register a handler that prints the message and another that counts messages. Print the passing messages as they arrive, then `Handled: <count>`.
inputFormat: Line 1 the minimum level; line 2 `n`; then `n` lines `LEVEL text`.
pseudocode:
INFO, WARN, ERROR
CLASS Logger
  private final Level min
  private final List<Consumer<String>> handlers = ArrayList<>()
  FUNCTION Logger(min)
    SET this.min = min
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION addHandler(h)
    CALL handlers.add(h)
  END FUNCTION
  FUNCTION log(level, text)
    IF level.compareTo(min) < 0 THEN
      RETURN
    END IF
    FOR Consumer<String> h : handlers
      CALL h.accept("[" + level + "] " + text)
    END FOR
  END FUNCTION
END CLASS
SET logger = Logger(Level.valueOf(the next word read))
SET count = all zeros
CALL logger.addHandler(print)
CALL logger.addHandler(msg => count[0]++)
READ n
FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1
  CALL logger.log(Level.valueOf(the next word read), the next word read)
END FOR
